messages:
ops-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected for customer LyraSystems in eu-west-1 (pool=lyra-pool-3). p95 3.1s (+1.8s), p99 9.8s (+7.4s). error rate normal. paging oncall.

maria: oncall here — acknowledged. pulling dashboards: https://console.redwood/observability/pool/lyra-pool-3

maria: @ajay can you join? going to grab traces & top tenants.

ajay: on it. seeing sustained tail for last ~12m. KV cache miss rate jumped to ~60% on long-context jobs. top contributor tenant_id=lyra-tenant-17 (~40% of recent QPS).

slo-bot: SLO ALERT: LyraSystems (enterprise) p99 > 5s for 10m. SLA flag: potential customer impact.

maria: running a quick diagnostic query to confirm distribution:
```sql
select percentile(latency_ms,95) as p95, percentile(latency_ms,99) as p99, count(*) from requests
where pool='lyra-pool-3' and region='eu-west-1' and ts > now() - interval '15 minutes';
```

ajay: query result: p95=3100ms, p99=9800ms, top tenant lyra-tenant-17. we also see larger seq-len requests causing KV churn.

tess: tagging in from SRE rotation — recommended immediate mitigation: tenant isolation (rate-limit), enable prefix caching, and spin up 2 warm spares in eu-west-1. fallback to smaller quantized model for sync routes if needed.

maria: agreed. mitigation plan: 1) apply tenant RPS cap to lyra-tenant-17 2) enable prefix/KV cache for that tenant 3) scale warm spares 4) prepare model-fallback rule for affected routes.

ajay: throttle command ready:
```bash
redwoodctl pools throttle --pool lyra-pool-3 --tenant lyra-tenant-17 --rps 20
```

maria: applying throttle now.

ops-bot: COMMAND OK — throttle applied. lyra-tenant-17 rps cap = 20.

darin-sre: observing queue depth drop. p99 improved to ~3.6s after ~90s. looks promising.

maria: spinning warm spares now:
```bash
redwoodctl autoscale --pool lyra-pool-3 --warm-spares 2 --region eu-west-1
```

ops-bot: AUTOSCALE accepted — estimated warm-up ~2m.

sam-cs: added to thread — I'll notify Lyra account team. who will send initial customer comms?

maria: @sam-cs pls send short heads-up: we applied temporary throttling and cache optimizations; performance trending back to baseline; ETA for full root-cause & follow-up later today.

ajay: enabling prefix/KV caching for lyra-tenant-17 now:
```bash
redwoodctl cache enable --tenant lyra-tenant-17 --prefix true
```

ops-bot: CACHE TOGGLE OK for lyra-tenant-17.

tess: update: after cache + throttle + warm spares p99=2.1s, p95=1.8s, throughput ~baseline. continuing to monitor for recurrence.

maria: creating incident ticket + runbook. JIRA INF-8421. actions logged: throttle, cache enable, warm-spares, fallback prepped.

maria: handing off monitoring to @tess for the night shift. next oncall midday = @ajay (09:00 UTC).

tess: taking handoff. short summary: single-tenant noise from lyra-tenant-17 caused KV churn and tail latency. mitigations applied (tenant throttle, prefix cache, 2 warm spares). fallback model ready but not activated. Will watch until 06:00 UTC and reopen thread if p99 > 5s.

sam-cs: sending customer note now: "We observed transient tail latency caused by heavy long-context usage from a single tenant. We've applied a temporary rate limit and caching improvements; latency has returned to baseline. We'll follow up with a full RCA and longer-term mitigation plan." Will CC account lead.

maria: thanks. for the postmortem, capture timeline, cache hit ratio before/after, KV miss windows, seq-length distribution, tenant QPS spike, and ops decisions. propose longer term: tenant-aware autoscaling thresholds + automatic model-fallback for long-context synchronous routes.

slo-bot: Incident INF-8421 created. Priority: P2. SLA impact: under review (possible credit exposure).

tess: marking thread monitored/standby. will re-open if we see >5s p99. :white_check_mark:
